coverageContext: Complete 47-term European-ancestry RBD research model; reported discrimination was modest (AUROC about0.61 for isolated RBD and0.60 for Parkinson disease with probable RBD). The primary paper's third comparison is Parkinson disease without probable RBD, although Catalog labels it probable RBD; retain this source discrepancy when reading evaluation records. The score did not predict age at onset or conversion to overt neurodegeneration. Not a sleep-study result, diagnosis, or prediction of future Parkinson disease or dementia.

Complete five-term childhood steroid-sensitive nephrotic-syndrome-weighted European research model. Evaluation AUROC0.638 contrasts548non-monogenic with49monogenic nephrotic-syndrome cases, not disease versus healthy population screening. The paper divided its score by possible allele count and discussed protective-allele recoding and cohort-specific proxies; GA retains the deposited alleles and natural-log weights unchanged, without normalization or proxies. Do not apply the paper's0.2threshold to GA raw sums. This cannot exclude a monogenic cause, predict steroid response, classify an individual kidney disorder, or guide treatment.
